chapters.title: The two ledgers
chapters.dek: Money on paper and money in the bank are different quantities, recorded at different moments. Almost everything else in the system is a consequence of that gap.

chapters.title: Debt between companies
chapters.dek: A receivable is a loan whether or not anyone calls it one. Limits, ageing, offsetting, and what a late payer legally owes.

chapters.title: Turning invoices into cash
chapters.dek: The supply chain finance products themselves: who starts each one, who carries the risk when it goes wrong, and what the money actually costs.

chapters.title: Planning and control
chapters.dek: Budgets, forecasts and approval rules — the part of the system that decides what is allowed to happen, before it happens.

chapters.title: Where the system meets the outside
chapters.dek: The bank, the tax authority and the auditor. Three outsiders whose disagreement with your data is always your problem to explain.

lessons.title: An invoice is not money
lessons.dek: Why invoices.status has no OPEN, why an issued invoice cannot be deleted, and how a single direction column decides which side of the books a row lands on.

lessons.title: Why you can never delete a financial record
lessons.dek: A financial row is not application state, it is evidence. Reversal, adjustment and replacement — the three legal ways to be wrong, and the two illegal ones.

lessons.title: Credit is not a score
lessons.dek: Limit, exposure and headroom are three different numbers people call the same thing. Plus what a score is for, and why blocking is usually the wrong action to attach to it.

lessons.title: Aging, and the debt that cancels itself
lessons.dek: One total tells you nothing; the same total split by age tells you everything. Then two-way offsetting under Điều 378, where a debt is settled without money moving.

lessons.title: Late-payment interest, the easiest thing here to code wrongly
lessons.dek: Why the 20% civil ceiling does not apply, why interest may never be charged on a penalty, and how one court precedent becomes two filters in code.

lessons.title: Three ways to turn an invoice into cash
lessons.dek: Invoice discounting, reverse factoring, inventory financing. The same problem solved three times, started by three different people, priced off three different credit ratings.

lessons.title: Recourse, collateral and the limit behind them
lessons.dek: Who pays when the buyer never does. With-recourse against without, what pledged stock is really worth, and why a financing limit moves on its own.

lessons.title: Comparing offers without being fooled by the headline
lessons.dek: The marketplace, the quotes it returns, and the arithmetic that turns "1.2% a month" and "a 3% discount for paying 60 days early" into two numbers you can actually compare.

lessons.title: A budget is not a forecast
lessons.dek: Plan, allocation, commitment, actual, variance — five states of the same đồng. And why budget control has to bite at approval rather than at payment.

lessons.title: Forecasting cash you do not have yet
lessons.dek: Why a cash forecast is built from due dates rather than trend lines, what a scenario is for, and how to set an alert threshold that is neither noise nor silence.

lessons.title: Who may sign, and who may not
lessons.dek: Segregation of duties, chief accountant against person in charge of accounting, and why a hard-coded approval chain deadlocks hundreds of thousands of perfectly legal micro-enterprises.

lessons.title: When the bank statement and the books disagree
lessons.dek: Reconciliation: what a statement line actually contains, why matching it to your own records is harder than it sounds, and what an unmatched line means by the end of the month.

lessons.title: Reading a set of financial statements in ten minutes
lessons.dek: Three sheets answering three different questions — what the company owns, what it earned, and where the cash went. Including the new name Thông tư 99/2025 gave the first of them.

lessons.title: Which books this company is required to keep
lessons.dek: Thông tư 99/2025 for everyone else, Thông tư 58/2026 for micro-enterprises, and the four tax methods that decide which screens a customer should never be shown.
